title: Yjs server loaded separate ESM and CommonJS instances
description: The custom ESM server imported Yjs directly while requiring y-websocket's CommonJS server utilities, which caused Yjs to detect two runtime instances.
error_message: Yjs was already imported. This breaks constructor checks and will lead to issues!
root_cause: An ESM Yjs import and the CommonJS import inside y-websocket resolved through different module entry points in the same process.
solution: Removed the ESM import and obtained Yjs with the same createRequire instance used for y-websocket utilities.

strategies: Use one module system for Yjs and its server protocol utilities within a process
Treat the Yjs duplicate-import warning as a blocking smoke-test failure
code_patterns: Avoid: ESM import of yjs beside required y-websocket/bin/utils
Use: const Y = require('yjs') with required y-websocket utilities
tests_to_add: Assert durable server startup output contains no duplicate Yjs warning

title: y-indexeddb leaves a rejected constructor chain when database open is refused
description: The storage-unavailable verification forced IndexedDB.open to fail. Although BoardPrep awaited a public provider operation and returned an unavailable fallback, y-indexeddb also creates an internal success-only promise chain whose rejection remained unhandled and terminated the Node verifier.

context.code_snippet: new IndexeddbPersistence(key, document) before an availability probe

error_message: Error: IndexedDB disabled for verification at lib0/indexeddb.openDB via IndexeddbPersistence constructor.
root_cause: y-indexeddb attaches an internal `.then(success)` without a rejection branch to its database-open promise, so open failure produces an additional unhandled rejected promise outside the caller-visible operation.
solution: Added a harmless empty-database availability probe that handles synchronous and asynchronous open refusal before constructing IndexeddbPersistence; unsupported storage now returns the in-memory fallback immediately.

strategies: Preflight browser storage APIs whose third-party wrappers do not fully own their rejection chains
Keep a deterministic disabled-storage test in the offline verification suite
code_patterns: Avoid: constructing IndexeddbPersistence before checking IndexedDB availability
Use: an explicit IDBOpenDBRequest probe with error and success handlers
tests_to_add: Verify disabled IndexedDB returns unavailable while in-memory Yjs editing remains functional

title: Browser WebSocket opened without completing the Yjs synced state
description: After an offline edit and reconnect, the authenticated browser socket reopened and exchanged Yjs and awareness frames, but the server did not answer the client's initial sync-step request, leaving provider.synced false and the UI in Connecting.

context.code_snippet: new WebsocketProvider(..., { connect: false, maxBackoffTime: 4000, params: {} })

error_message: Browser acceptance timed out waiting for Live sync active while the WebSocket remained open and provider.synced stayed false.
root_cause: The initial browser sync-step request can be lost around connection setup; with the provider's default zero resync interval, no later state-vector request repairs the incomplete handshake.
solution: Enabled the provider's built-in 2.5-second resync interval so an open connection retries the Yjs state-vector handshake while preserving the same document and editor.

strategies: Exercise offline-to-online transitions in a real browser in addition to Node WebSocket integration tests
Configure a bounded Yjs resync interval for long-lived collaborative clients
code_patterns: Avoid: relying on a single initial sync request for a long-lived browser provider
Use: resyncInterval with the stable WebsocketProvider
tests_to_add: Keep browser acceptance coverage for Offline to Connecting to Live transitions

title: Root layout omitted Next's smooth-scroll transition marker
description: Browser verification found Next's development warning because global CSS enables smooth scrolling but the root html element did not declare the framework marker.
error_message: Detected scroll-behavior: smooth on the html element. Add data-scroll-behavior="smooth".
root_cause: The visual system's smooth-scroll CSS was added without the corresponding Next route-transition declaration on the document root.
solution: Added data-scroll-behavior="smooth" to the root html element.

strategies: Treat browser console warnings as part of the UI verification gate
Keep framework-required document attributes next to root layout concerns
code_patterns: Avoid: smooth html scrolling without the framework marker
tests_to_add: Assert browser verification has no application or framework warnings

title: Room Server Action module exported a non-function value
description: Creating a room reached the root App Router error boundary. The active Next development log reports that a `use server` file exported an object; the room action module exports `INITIAL_ROOM_ACTION_STATE` alongside its async Server Actions and both room client components import that object.

context.code_snippet: export const INITIAL_ROOM_ACTION_STATE: RoomActionState = { message: '', status: 'idle' };

error_message: Error: A "use server" file can only export async functions, found object.
root_cause: Next.js treats every export from a module-level `use server` file as a Server Function export. The shared initial action-state object violates that runtime contract even though the production TypeScript/build gate did not expose it.
solution: Moved RoomActionState and INITIAL_ROOM_ACTION_STATE into a neutral action-state module, updated both client form components to import state there, and left src/app/rooms/actions.ts with async function runtime exports only.

strategies: Keep module-level `use server` files limited to async function exports
Exercise authenticated Server Action pages in the active development runtime in addition to production build checks
code_patterns: Avoid: export const INITIAL_STATE = {...} from a module-level `use server` file
Use: export shared state from a neutral module and import it separately in client components
tests_to_add: Load the authenticated room dashboard and create a room in the Next development runtime
Assert the development log contains no invalid-use-server-value error
